title: The Dertogada Canonical Pentology
excerpt: A deep exploration of the five interconnected speculative volumes spanning Dertogada, Ramatohara, Xantoxara, Yoratorad, and Yotod.
body:
The Dertogada literary universe represents a landmark milestone in modern Ethiopian speculative literature. Beginning with the publication of Dertogada in 2009 (2001 E.C.) by Yismake Worku at age 22, the series explores subterranean research sanctuaries beneath Lake Tana, sovereign quantum mechanics, international counter-espionage, and ancient Ethiopian ecclesiastical scholarship.

Over the course of five canonical volumes—Dertogada, Ramatohara, Xantoxara, Yoratorad, and Yotod—the narrative follows protagonists including engineer Shagiz Ejigu, Zipporah, and Dr. Anania as they navigate geopolitical tension, cyber sovereignty, and the moral responsibilities of technological discovery.

title: The Lost Spell (Kebur Dengay) Shortlisted for UK Translation Prize
excerpt: English translation by Dr. Bethlehem Attfield published by Henningham Family Press shortlisted for the 2022 TA First Translation Prize.
body:
Yismake Worku's celebrated novel 'Kebur Dengay' (ክቡር ድንጋይ), translated into English as 'The Lost Spell' by Dr. Bethlehem Attfield and published in the United Kingdom by Henningham Family Press, was officially shortlisted for the prestigious 2022 TA First Translation Prize.

The novel combines biting political satire, Ethiopian magical realism, and philosophical introspection through the transformation of its protagonist into an African bird, offering acute observations on governance, nature, and human vulnerability.

title: Brana & Orbit: The Tana Manuscript Observatory
excerpt: The official digital literary archive and interactive exhibition for Yismake Worku is now live.
body:
We are proud to present the official digital literary exhibition for Yismake Worku: 'Brana & Orbit: The Tana Manuscript Observatory'.

Featuring authentic Amharic typography (Noto Serif Ethiopic), complete bibliography verification, the Dertogada constellation map, and archival records, this platform bridges 1,500 years of Ethiopian monastic manuscript codicology with visionary Afrofuturist speculation.
